profile.headline: Retired - Senior Embedded Software Engineer at Analog Devices
profile.summary:
•	Over 15 years of experiences in networking design, architect, and development software/firmware on embedded platforms, routers, switches, IBM BladeCenter Advanced Management Module, and IBM Chassis System.
•	Major strength in decision making, planning/organizing, software development, problem solving, team building and communications. 
•	Networking team lead of IBM Chassis Management Module in PureFlex Chassis System and has written many Design Documentations.
•	Very strong skill in C language. Very experiences in embedded real-time operating systems, embedded software, multi-threaded system, chip driver, Linux kernel.
•	Very strong understanding and deep knowledge of Ethernet frame, VLAN, ARP, IP, TCP/UDP, NTP, SNMP, DHCP, DNS and HTTP.
•	A creative innovative problem solver, deep technical knowledge in networking and a proven ability to design and architect network, develop software, solve problems and produces quality and achieves consistent results.
•	Familiar and proficient in embedded systems Linux, Nucleus, VxWork. 
•	Familiar with tools GIT, SVN, Eclipse, Clearcase, PHP, Perl, Python, Scripts.
•	Experiences with working with customers, vendors, and partners to solve critical and time demand problems, features.
•	Very creative ideas and innovations led to co-authored of 7 patents and several publications.

positions.title: Senior Firmware Embedded Engineer
positions.description:
•	Technical leader of the Advanced Management Module networking team and ownership of the embedded platforms networking components in the IBM eServer-Xseries BladeCenter.
•	Design and architect for Advanced Management Module networking features, customers’ and vendors’ requirements.
•	Provide networking support, validate, and responsible for all Switch Modules (BNT, Cisco, Voltair, QLogic) and Blade Daughter cards on IBM BladeCenter.
•	Design and architect the IPV6 on Advanced Management Module embedded platforms. Provide technical support on IPV6 questions and implementations.
•	Designed and implemented software/firmware for network architecture.
•	Implemented network infrastructure, developed network switch driver, and other network features like Serial over LAN, Redundant failover, TCP Command Mode, Channel Manager.

patents.title: Establishing communication between entities in a shared network
patents.description: A method, system, and/or computer program product establishes a communication session between two entities on a shared network. A request to locate a desired entity on a shared network, which hosts one or more entities that are unknown to a requesting entity, is received from the requesting entity. A desired environment with which the desired entity is associated is selected by the requesting entity. An inquiry packet is broadcast to all entities on the shared network. The inquiry packet, which does not specify a data link layer by which any particular entity communicates with the shared network, includes a request for an identity of any entity on the shared network that is assigned to the desired environment. A response to the inquiry packet provides an identity and data link layer address of the desired entity, thus enabling the establishment of a communication session between the requesting and desired entities.

patents.title: Autoconfiguration Of An IPv6 Component In A Segmented Network
patents.description: Autoconfiguration of an IPv6 component in a segmented network including receiving an IPv6 packet; determining whether the received IPv6 packet is a router advertisement or a router solicitation; if the received IPv6 packet is a router advertisement, then retrieving through an out-of-band link a MAC address for the IPv6 component, removing a MAC address of a sending router, inserting in the packet instead an internal MAC address for forwarding packets to the IPv6 component, removing a multicast destination MAC address, inserting in the packet the destination MAC address of the IPv6 component, and forwarding the packet to the IPv6 component as a unicast message; if the received IPv6 packet is a router solicitation, then removing the MAC address of the sending IPv6 component, inserting in the packet instead an external MAC address for forwarding packets to the router, and forwarding the packet to the router as a multicast message.
